long_review.hot_take: Bullwaves launched in 2023 with a Seychelles licence and immediately started collecting awards and affiliate partnerships faster than it collected a verifiable track record. The commission-free ECN model sounds attractive on paper — but when your Trustpilot profile gets flagged by the platform itself for suspected fake review patterns, and independent reviewers find your website full of dead links and misinformation, the pricing model stops being the story. The story becomes: can you get your money out? And after less than three years, there is simply not enough public evidence to answer that question with confidence.

sections.heading: Is Bullwaves Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Launched in 2023 under an FSA Seychelles licence, Bullwaves is attempting to carve out space in an extremely crowded offshore broker market. The pitch: commission-free ECN trading from 0.1 pips on MetaTrader 5, plus a prop firm (Bullwaves Prime) that funds traders up to $2 million. On paper, the value proposition has elements that stand out — particularly the zero-commission ECN model that most competitors do not offer.

But the flags accumulate quickly. DayTrading.com — a generally balanced review site — described the Bullwaves website as 'full of misinformation and dead links' with 'weak regulatory credentials that raise questions about reliability.' Their Trustpilot profile received an official platform warning for suspected fake review patterns. TradersUnion gives a 5.62/10 moderate-risk rating. FXEmpire rated deposits and withdrawals at 2.0 out of 5. And WikiFX conducted an on-site office verification that raises further questions about operational transparency.

Is it a scam? There is no evidence of that. Is it a broker NAFT can confidently recommend? No. Not yet. The operating history is too thin and the independent signals too mixed.

sections.heading: Is Bullwaves Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
One licence. Offshore. No investor compensation. Bullwaves operates as Equitex Capital Limited, registered in Seychelles (Registration No. 8434948-1), holding FSA Seychelles Securities Dealer licence SD185. That is the entire regulatory picture. There is no FCA entity. No CySEC entity. No ASIC entity. No NFA registration. The FSA Seychelles is a Tier-3 regulator — it requires fund segregation in theory but has extremely limited enforcement capacity for individual retail complaints. If Bullwaves fails or refuses a withdrawal, your practical recourse is close to zero.

The broker states funds are held in segregated accounts, but does not name the custodian bank. No negative balance protection details are published beyond basic statements. No investor compensation scheme exists under FSA Seychelles — if the broker becomes insolvent, client funds have no guaranteed recovery path. This is the fundamental risk of any Seychelles-only broker, and Bullwaves is no exception.

sections.heading: Who Can Open an Account With Bullwaves? — Accepted Countries and Restrictions
sections.body:
Accepted: Most countries globally — Bullwaves operates a wide-open onboarding policy typical of Seychelles-registered brokers.

Not accepted: United States, Belgium, North Korea, Afghanistan, Belarus, Central African Republic, China, Cuba, Libya, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Palestine.

The exclusion list is minimal — essentially OFAC-sanctioned countries plus Belgium and the US. This means traders in the EU, UK, and Australia can technically open accounts, but they receive zero local regulatory protection by doing so. A UK trader choosing Bullwaves over an FCA-regulated broker is voluntarily giving up FSCS compensation and FCA dispute resolution.
sections.practical_note: All clients route to the single Seychelles entity. No local regulatory protection regardless of where you live. If you have access to Tier-1 regulated brokers in your country, choosing Bullwaves means accepting materially higher counterparty risk for potentially lower trading costs.

sections.heading: Bullwaves Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Three account types, all commission-free — which is the unusual element here. The Classic account starts at $100 minimum with spreads from 1.6 pips EUR/USD — that is $16 per standard lot all-in, which is expensive by any standard. The VIP account at $3,000 minimum brings spreads down to 0.8 pips ($8/lot). The ECN account at $5,000 minimum offers 0.1 pips with zero commission — a claimed all-in cost of approximately $1 per lot.

That ECN pricing is genuinely unusual. Most brokers offering 0.1 pip spreads charge $5-$7 per lot in commission on top. Bullwaves claims zero. The question is how they profit on that tier — likely through wider spreads during volatile sessions or through the spread markup being embedded differently than stated minimums suggest. TradersUnion reports actual EUR/USD spreads of 0.2-0.6 pips on what they call the Standard account, which is more realistic than the 0.1 minimum.

Inactivity fee is $10 per year — lower than most competitors. A EUR 10 fee applies to bank wire withdrawals below EUR 100. No custody fees or account maintenance fees disclosed.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of Bullwaves?
sections.body:
Limited payment options: Visa, Mastercard, bank wire, and Neteller. No crypto deposits. No Skrill. Deposits are instant via card. Withdrawals are stated to take 1-5 business days — a wide window that suggests processing is not automated.

Bullwaves enforces a strict withdrawal routing policy: card deposits must be withdrawn back to the same card first before any alternative method is used. Bank wire withdrawals require a bank statement proving account ownership before approval. This creates additional friction — particularly for first-time withdrawals. A EUR 10 fee applies to bank wire withdrawals of EUR 100 or less.

FXEmpire rated Bullwaves 2.0/5 on deposits and withdrawals — the lowest category score in their review. The reason: limited options, the routing restriction, and the fee structure. There is insufficient public data to confirm whether the 1-5 day window is consistently met.

sections.heading: Bullwaves Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Insufficient public evidence to paint a clear picture — and that itself is the picture. Bullwaves has operated for less than three years. The volume of publicly available withdrawal experience reports is thin compared to established brokers. What exists is mixed: some users report successful withdrawals within the stated timeframe, while FXEmpire's low 2.0/5 deposit/withdrawal score suggests the process is not consistently smooth.

The withdrawal routing restriction adds friction that newer traders may not expect. You deposit via Visa, you must withdraw to that same Visa first — even if you later want to use bank wire for profits. This is not unusual in the industry (anti-money-laundering compliance), but combined with the bank statement requirement for wire withdrawals, the first withdrawal experience may take longer than advertised.

If your withdrawal stalls: contact support at support@bullwaves.com or call +248 4373840. There is no external dispute resolution body that Bullwaves is a member of. Your escalation path is limited to the FSA Seychelles directly — a regulator with minimal enforcement capacity for individual retail complaints. This is the practical reality of offshore-only regulation.

DayTrading.com — an independent review site — described the Bullwaves website as 'full of misinformation and dead links' with 'weak regulatory credentials that raise questions about reliability.' This is an unusual level of criticism from a site that typically maintains neutral language.

WikiFX conducted an on-site office verification at the claimed Cyprus address — the findings raise questions about operational transparency and physical presence.
No Tier-1 regulatory licence anywhere in the group structure. FSA Seychelles (SD185) is the only licence. No investor compensation scheme exists. No external dispute resolution membership.

The ECN account claims 0.1 pip spreads with zero commission — an unusually profitable offering for the broker that requires explanation. If the broker is not charging commission on raw spreads, how do they profit on that tier? The economics are unclear.

sections.heading: Who Should Use Bullwaves — and Who Should Not
sections.body: The honest answer: very few traders should choose this broker at this stage.
not_for: Anyone who values capital safety — there is no investor compensation under FSA Seychelles and insufficient track record to assess reliability.
Traders with access to Tier-1 regulated brokers offering similar pricing — Pepperstone, IC Markets, and Exness all offer raw spreads with established track records.
Beginners — combining a new broker, offshore regulation, 1:500 leverage, and no safety net is a recipe for capital destruction.
Anyone planning to deposit more than they can afford to lose entirely — the risk profile does not support large deposits at this stage.
Traders who rely on MetaTrader 4 — only MT5 is available.
for: Experienced traders specifically testing the commission-free ECN model with small capital they can afford to lose.
Prop firm traders using Bullwaves Prime who want consistency between their funded and retail accounts.
Traders in regions with no access to Tier-1 brokers who have exhausted all better-regulated alternatives first.

sections.heading: How to Open a Bullwaves Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Standard offshore onboarding — fast but with less regulatory friction than Tier-1 brokers.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit bullwaves.com, click Open Account, provide email, country, and basic personal details. Choose your account type (Classic, VIP, or ECN). The process takes under 5 minutes.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload government-issued ID and proof of address. Bullwaves uses Sumsub for verification — processing is typically within 24 hours. Your account will not be fully activated until KYC is approved.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit via card (instant) or bank wire. Start with the minimum amount. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately — before adding more capital. If it processes within the stated 1-5 day window, you have a data point. If it does not, you have your answer.

sections.practical_note: Make a small deposit. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly, scale with confidence.

sections.heading: Bullwaves Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Bullwaves 4.2 out of 10 in May 2026. The commission-free ECN pricing model is genuinely interesting and worth monitoring — if spreads hold at 0.1 pips with zero commission, it would be one of the most cost-effective offerings in the market. But pricing alone does not build trust. Trust requires time, transparency, and a verifiable withdrawal track record. Bullwaves has operated for less than three years, holds only an FSA Seychelles licence, and has accumulated multiple independent red flags including a Trustpilot platform warning and website quality criticisms.

The risks are specific: no investor compensation, no external dispute resolution, no Tier-1 oversight, no published retail loss rate, and insufficient public evidence to confirm whether the withdrawal process works consistently at scale. These are not theoretical concerns — they are the practical realities of depositing with a new offshore broker.

NAFT cannot recommend Bullwaves at this time. If you are considering this broker, deposit only what you can afford to lose entirely, test the withdrawal pipeline before scaling, and have a Tier-1 alternative ready. Exness, IC Markets, and Pepperstone all offer competitive raw spreads with decades of track record and real regulatory protection. Use those first.
